content.content: Your task is to implement and verify the dequeue (pop) operation for a Ring Buffer data structure. Because the ring buffer uses a fixed-size underlying array, the "front" of the queue is not fixed at the array's index 0 but is instead tracked by a moving head pointer. Verification: Verify that the operation returns the element currently at the "front" of the logical sequence (index 0). Structural Update: You must prove that after the element is returned, the new model sequence is shortened by one and contains the remaining elements in their original relative order. Difference from Standard Queue: Unlike a standard Vec-based queue where popping from the front requires shifting all subsequent elements (an $O(N)$ operation), verify that this operation achieves the same result by simply advancing the internal head pointer (an $O(1)$ operation), correctly wrapping around to the start of the array if the end is reached. ---- 1 use vstd::prelude::*; 2 3 verus! { 4 // Following is the block for necessary definitions 5 // 6 // A RingBuffer wrapper around a Vec 7 struct RingBuffer { 8 pub data: Vec, 9 pub head: usize, 10 pub len: usize, 11 pub capacity: usize, 12 } 13 14 impl RingBuffer { 15 pub open spec fn view(&self) -> Seq { 16 Seq::new(self.len as nat, |i: int| 17 self.data.view()[(self.head as int + i) % self.capacity as int] 18 ) 19 } 20 21 pub open spec fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { 22 &&& self.capacity > 0 23 &&& self.data.view().len() == self.capacity as nat 24 &&& self.len <= self.capacity 25 &&& self.head < self.capacity 26 } 27 28 pub fn new(capacity: usize, fill_value: T) -> (s: Self) 29 requires capacity > 0 30 ensures 31 s.is_valid(), 32 s.view().len() == 0, 33 s.capacity == capacity, 34 { 35 let mut data = Vec::with_capacity(capacity); 36 let mut i = 0; 37 while i < capacity 38 invariant 39 data.view().len() == i as nat, 40 i <= capacity, 41 { 42 data.push(fill_value); 43 i = i + 1; 44 } 45 RingBuffer { data, head: 0, len: 0, capacity } 46 } 47 // 48 49 // Following is the block for potential helper specifications 50 // 51 52 // 53 54 // Following is the block for proofs of lemmas, or functions that help the implementation or verification of the main specification 55 // 56 57 // 58 59 // Following is the block for the main specification 60 // 61 // Pop the oldest element from the buffer 62 pub fn dequeue(&mut self) -> (val: T) 63 requires 64 old(self).is_valid(), 65 old(self).len > 0, 66 ensures 67 self.is_valid(), 68 val == old(self).view()[0], 69 self.view() == old(self).view().drop_first(), 70 // 71 // 72 { 73 74 } 75 // 76 } 77 78 fn main() {} 79 80 }description.md ringbuffer_dequeue.rs
